purpose: Close scoring seams before Product #7 certification by requiring variant-grain classification, positive semantic-correctness verification, and a deterministic instance-versus-structural-shape discriminator.

variant_grain_rule.principle: ProductSemantic maturity and repeatability scoring are evaluated at concept plus semantic-variant plus product plus version grain. A green result for one variant cannot be projected onto another variant.

instance_vs_structural_shape_discriminat.classification_time: before Product #7 certification outcome is known

all_conditions_required: Every asserted semantic field maps one-to-one to a field or relation already present in a governed baseline schema or typed contract.
Values are literals, registered enumerations, identifiers, evidence references, or repeated instances of an already-supported record shape.
No new conditional evaluation, precedence, selection, aggregation, transformation, fallback, derivation, or composition rule is required to interpret the record.
The frozen baseline binder and certifier validate the intended semantic meaning, not merely accept the serialized fields.
examples: Changing a fixed copayment rate from an existing value to 5 percent while using the same rate, basis, and scope fields is an instance.
Creating separate waiting-period records for 24-month and 48-month condition groups using an already-supported scalar waiting-period shape is an instance.

any_condition_sufficient: A new field, relation, cardinality, semantic composition, or governed declarative schema shape is required.
Configuration contains selectors, conditionals, precedence, ordering, derived values, fallback logic, or other decision logic needed to choose or compute the semantic outcome.
The baseline schema can store the values but the baseline binder or certifier cannot validate the intended semantic meaning without new interpretation logic.
A previously unsupported interaction among existing fields changes their meaning or applicability rather than merely supplying new values.
STRUCTURAL_SHAPE.classification_consequence: A required structural shape is CONFIG_SPEC only when it is purely declarative and contains no executable or hidden decision logic; otherwise it is a REPRESENTATION_GAP or a protocol metric failure as applicable.

instance_vs_structural_shape_discriminat.tie_break_rule: If reasonable reviewers disagree whether a change is INSTANCE or STRUCTURAL_SHAPE, classify it as STRUCTURAL_SHAPE for repeatability scoring until the ambiguity is resolved against the frozen baseline.

positive_semantic_correctness_gate.scope: every certified Product #7 claim, not a sample
positive_semantic_correctness_gate.requirement: Each certified claim must be manually or deterministically spot-checked against the exact authoritative source span and recorded as semantically faithful across every material asserted dimension.
positive_semantic_correctness_gate.failure_rule: Any unresolved semantic mismatch blocks REUSE/CONFIG_SPEC for that claim or variant even when exact hash lineage is present and all absence metrics remain zero.

concept_aggregation_rule.REUSE: A target concept is REUSE only if every required observed Product #7 variant for that concept is REUSE and passes the positive semantic-correctness gate.
concept_aggregation_rule.CONFIG_SPEC: A target concept is CONFIG_SPEC when every required observed variant is REUSE or CONFIG_SPEC, at least one is CONFIG_SPEC, none is REPRESENTATION_GAP or KNOWLEDGE_GAP, and every certified claim passes the positive semantic-correctness gate.
concept_aggregation_rule.REPRESENTATION_GAP: A target concept is REPRESENTATION_GAP when any required observed variant has authoritative evidence but cannot be faithfully represented and certified by the frozen baseline under the discriminator.
concept_aggregation_rule.KNOWLEDGE_GAP: A target concept is KNOWLEDGE_GAP when any required observed variant lacks sufficient authoritative/corroborating evidence and no stronger failure applies.

repeatability_verdict_guard.note: A mixed variant result can be a valid and valuable experiment outcome without constituting STRONG_REPEATABILITY_PROVEN or MINIMUM_REPEATABILITY_PROVEN.

test_count_governance.rule: No repeatability or milestone result may cite a test count that cannot be reproduced from the referenced Git-controlled commit and declared dependency environment.
